articles.title: TVS Family Partition Suit: What Is Lakshmi Venu Seeking? Exclusive With C Aryama Sundaram
articles.description: The TVS family is facing a legal dispute over the partition of joint family assets, with Dr Lakshmi Venu approaching the Madras High Court seeking her rightful share in the family property. The suit follows a partition notice sent to her father, Venu Srinivasan, on 16 November 2026, after efforts to reach an amicable resolution failed. Dr Lakshmi Venu has also sought access to documents and information relating to the family assets, which she says have been consistently withheld despite multiple requests. In an exclusive conversation with Business Today, C Aryama Sundaram, counsel for Dr Lakshmi Venu, discusses the legal case, the demand for partition, the rights being asserted and the issues at the heart of the family dispute. The suit concerns ownership of joint family assets and is not directed at the operations of any TVS company. Mrs Mallika Srinivasan has also publicly backed her daughter's right to an equal share in the family assets. What does the legal battle mean for the TVS family, and what happens next? Watch the exclusive conversation for more.

articles.title: Cabinet approves Rs 11,000 cr scheme to boost construction equipment manufacturing amid China woes
articles.description: The Union Cabinet on Wednesday approved an Rs 11,000 crore scheme to boost domestic manufacturing of construction and infrastructure equipment (CIE), as concerns grow over India's dependence on China for critical machinery and components used in major infrastructure projects. The eight-year scheme, running from FY27 to FY34, seeks to strengthen India's construction equipment manufacturing ecosystem, reduce reliance on imports and make domestic manufacturers more competitive in global markets.

Audi India announces hike in vehicle prices by up to 2% from January 1
articles.description: German luxury carmaker Audi on Tuesday said it will increase ex-showroom prices of its models in India by up to 2 per cent with effect from January 1, 2027, to offset rising input costs. The latest hike marks Audi India's second price revision in 2026, as the automaker had previously raised prices by up to 2 per cent across its model range from April 1 this year. The price revision will be applicable across its model range, the company said in a statement. "In response to rising input costs, we will be implementing a price revision of up to 2 per cent. This adjustment is essential to maintaining the long-term sustainability of our business. We have kept this revision as measured as possible, and our focus remains on giving customers an ownership experience that solidifies their trust in the brand," Audi India Brand Director Balbir Singh Dhillon said.
